subject.title: feat(android): per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should Android accept arbitrary per-gateway custom proxy headers sent before Gateway authentication, or should this surface be narrowed to typed proxy-auth credentials first?
rationale: The source gap is real, but arbitrary operator-defined headers become persistent secrets and are replayed on the WebSocket upgrade before OpenClaw Gateway auth runs, so automation cannot choose the permanent security/product boundary.

options.title: Approve arbitrary headers after proof
options.body: Land this Android slice after owner/security reviewers approve the sanitizer, secure-store lifecycle, redaction, TLS-only behavior, gateway-only attachment, and real Android proof.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth
options.body: Revise the PR to a smaller Basic/Bearer/fixed-header credential model if maintainers do not want a general name/value header store in Android settings.

options.title: Pause for shared mobile policy
options.body: Hold the Android PR until the canonical issue and iOS sibling settle one cross-platform mobile proxy credential contract.

recommendation.title: Approve arbitrary headers after proof
recommendation.body: Land this Android slice after owner/security reviewers approve the sanitizer, secure-store lifecycle, redaction, TLS-only behavior, gateway-only attachment, and real Android proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the current PR and canonical issue and has the strongest current history on the Android gateway auth/security boundary.
